Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Martin Lorenz is emeritus, so he is not counted as an ordinary new-student adviser.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A bachelor’s is sufficient; no master’s required. A mathematics major or equivalent should include abstract
algebra, real analysis and advanced work in the intended area. CST recommends GPA3.0 but considers lower
GPAs holistically. UChicago mathematics is an eligible degree route; conferral and individual preparation still
matter. [s1] [s2] [s4]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Start the Temple application and choose Mathematics PhD. No advance adviser agreement is required. For a
fee waiver, first upload the statement, resume and unofficial transcripts, then email the Graduate Chair with
the reason. Confirm the English waiver while the UChicago degree is unfinished. [s1] [s13]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No adviser agreement needed before applying; selection generally occurs in year2. Lang welcomes a
statement of interest but explicitly does not meet applicants before acceptance. Current chair/contact
information should come from the live roster, not the older brochure. [s1] [s18] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use the online application linked by Mathematics and the status checklist. No account was created, so
portal-only essay prompts and referee controls remain open verification items. [s1] [s5] [s6]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
CST explicitly has 2027 applications open; Mathematics publishes standing December 15/December 1 dates.
The catalog is 2026-27 and the available union pay schedule ends 2025-26. These are not interchangeable
with 2027-28 financial terms. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s11]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Standing rule]
December 15 for full consideration (standing date; year and time zone not explicitly attached). CST explicitly
says 2027 applications are open. Applications after December 15 may be reviewed case by case; no final late
cutoff is promised. [s1] [s3]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
December 15 full-consideration target; full-time applicants receive automatic assistantship consideration.
Need-based application-fee waiver requests have December 1 priority, decisions before December 15.
University fellowship nominations are departmental, with no applicant-facing 2027 cutoff established. [s1] [s4]
[s9]

Reference receipt [Unresolved]
A separate final letter deadline/grace period is not published on the mathematics pages. Arrange all three for
December 15; obtain explicit permission before relying on later receipt. [s1] [s2]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
No separate score grace period established. If English testing is needed, aim for official receipt by the
full-consideration deadline; Math GRE is optional and General GRE is not considered. [s1] [s13]
Supporting documents [Conflict]
Aim for a complete December 15 file. Official transcripts: CST says when accepting an offer; Mathematics and
the international instructions say before/at matriculation. Resolve this timing difference after admission;
unofficial records suffice for review. [s1] [s4] [s13]
Accepting an offer [Conflict]
No mathematics-specific fall 2027 response date was established. Public pages also disagree on a general
minimum deposit (USD200 versus100); neither establishes a mathematics deposit. Obtain the actual
response/deposit terms from the offer. [s7] [s8]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Central current minima: TOEFL4.5 for tests from January 21, 2026 (older test79), IELTS6.5, PTE53, DET110 or
LanguageCert70. Mathematics still displays the older TOEFL scale and four-test list. Use the central new-scale
rule and check any program-specific exception. [s13] [s1]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Mathematics exempts English-medium undergraduate education; central policy exempts a completed US
undergraduate degree. Thus a completed UChicago degree qualifies. Whether the portal grants the waiver
before conferral is not explicit. Separate TA spoken-English certification remains to be verified. [s1] [s13]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required and explicitly not considered. [s1] [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional; no published minimum or recommendation strength beyond optional. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload unofficial transcripts from all postsecondary institutions, including transfer work. Final official records
and degree certificates are needed after admission. English translations must be institutional or ATA-certified
for non-English records. The China/India additional-document rules concern education there; citizenship alone
does not turn a UChicago degree into a foreign degree. [s4] [s13]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No separate document is specified in the mathematics admissions checklist/bulletin. Optional-upload
permission, template and length are not established publicly. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Current resume required. No mathematics-specific page limit, formatting or file-size rule is public; follow the
portal’s upload specification. [s1]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required statement of goals,500-1000words in the bulletin. Prompt paraphrase: explain your academic path
and Temple goals, motivation, research/rigorous self-study, career plans and departmental fit; add relevant
context not otherwise explained. Font/spacing/file format are not specified publicly. [s2] [s1]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
The fee-waiver instructions call the required goals statement a personal statement; no second separate
background essay is listed. Check the live form for additional questions rather than duplicating the same
statement automatically. [s1] [s2]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Research fit and prior research/self-study belong in the goals statement. A separate research-interest essay is
not listed. [s1] [s2]
Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary; Publications list; Course-list
document; Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
Not separately specified on the public mathematics checklist/bulletin. Live-form requirement/optional status,
prompt, length, format and permission to upload/link remain unverified. [s1] [s2]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
No separate admission-funding essay is listed for automatic assistantship consideration. Fellowship
nominations may require additional information; exact nominee questions, limits and attachments were not
found publicly. Fee-waiver email must explain financial need. [s4] [s9] [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Fall 2027 stipend not yet established. The linked 2022-26 union agreement sets a 2025-26 minimum
USD27,000 for a nine-month appointment; this is historical, not a 2027 guarantee. Mathematics promises
tuition remission and benefits but some student fees remain. Its “full-year salary” wording does not identify a
specific twelve-month stipend; ask for the actual offer and summer terms. [s11] [s1]
Years of support [Conflict]
Current department admissions promises at least five years, conditional on satisfactory progress. Older
handbook language says most students are funded and rare unfunded admissions occur; get the written
five-year guarantee in the offer. [s1] [s10]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Full-time applicants are automatically considered for assistantships, with no published citizenship exclusion.
F-1 students do not qualify for the federal aid category limited to US citizens/permanent residents.
International students must maintain qualifying health insurance. [s4]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Support normally takes TA/RA or fellowship form. Handbook requires GPA>=3.25 for assistantships. Bulletin
tuition support is capped at nine credits per term under the standard appointment; verify coverage for the
planned load. Current contract/summer/work terms must be confirmed for 2027. [s10] [s2] [s11]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate assistantship application for full-time applicants. University fellowships require departmental
nomination; self-nomination is not allowed. [s4] [s9]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
University fellowships and faculty research assistantships; ScholarshipUniverse lists external opportunities,
each with its own eligibility and deadlines. No universal additional 2027 amount is published. [s4] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD60 online application; paper applications are listed at 75 but the online mathematics route should be used.
[s7] [s8]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Limited need-based departmental waivers: create an application, upload statement/resume/unofficial
transcripts, then email the current Graduate Chair explaining need. December 1 is priority; decisions before
December 15; later requests considered rolling. No international exclusion is stated, but approval is
discretionary. [s1]

routes and outdated personnel, so it is not used as current submission authority. [s1] [s4] [s7] [s8] [s10] [s12] [s13]

deposit/response date; fellowship nominee requirements; faculty openings.

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Number theory
Jaclyn Lang
p-adic modular forms, Galois representations, Eisenstein ideals and arithmetic geometry. [s14] [s15] [s16] [s17]
[s18]
Assistant Professor on current official site; generally open to advising, but no preacceptance applicant meetings.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · A new perspective on the rank of Mazur’s Eisenstein Hecke algebra
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Ari Shnidman
Arithmetic statistics, rational points, abelian varieties, modular curves and L-values. [s14] [s15] [s19] [s20] [s21]
Associate Professor since 2025 on current institutional/personal records; fall 2027 opening unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Exceptional points on Atkin-Lehner quotients
With Eran Assaf and Sachi Hashimoto; primary paper linked from current research record.
Representation theory
Vasily Dolgushev
Grothendieck-Teichmueller theory, operads and Galois actions; an algebra/geometry connection rather than a
conventional automorphic-representation specialization. [s14] [s22] [s23] [s24]
Professor on current Temple pages; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2024 preprint, revised August 2026 · Accessing non-abelian quotients of the Grothendieck-Teichmueller
group via elementary tools
